references.text: Matthew's parallel account where Jesus called the twelve disciples to himself and gave them authority over unclean spirits to drive them out, and to heal every disease and every affliction.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus called the twelve to himself and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over the unclean spirits.
Jesus had previously chosen the twelve apostles, who are now gathered here in 9:1 to receive authority and power.
Later, the Lord also appointed seventy others and sent them out, showing an expansion of the mission that began with the twelve in 9:1.
The seventy received a similar commission to heal the sick, paralleling the authority given to the twelve in 9:1.
Jesus gave the disciples specific instructions to heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, and drive out demons—an elaboration of the power granted in Luke 9:1.
Jesus appointed the twelve so that they might be with him and so that he could send them out to preach and have authority to drive out demons.
Jesus promised that signs would follow those who believe: they would drive out demons and lay hands on the sick, who would then recover—a confirmation of the authority given in Luke 9:1.
The apostles received a promise of power when the Holy Spirit came upon them, which is a continuation of the power Jesus gave them in Luke 9:1.
The disciples went out and carried out the mission they received in verse 1: they traveled from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing everywhere.
